domain: planning a week of outfits including a wedding ceremony under everyday-casuals daily uniform
base_instruction: You are a personal styling advisor AI. Help the user plan their weekly outfits.

state_queue.anchor: I need to plan my outfits for next week — Monday through Friday.

flow_info.value: Monday: regular day at the coworking space, afternoon coffee with a friend.
Tuesday: working from home all day, video calls with teammates in the morning.
Wednesday: attending my cousin's wedding ceremony at a cathedral in the afternoon, reception dinner immediately after at a formal venue. Invitation says black-tie.
Thursday: team lunch at a casual bistro, then errands around the neighborhood.
Friday: wrapping up the week at the coworking space, happy hour drinks with coworkers after.

hidden_state.value: You are planning outfits for Monday through Friday. You state your everyday-casuals uniform preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each day's activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the casual uniform preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me put together the full week' — do not enumerate the days, do not ask 'can I wear my usual for all five days', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe your uniform works for everything. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and matter-of-fact. State each day's plan in 1-2 short sentences. No anxiety, no hedging, no fashion enthusiasm. Tone of someone casually listing their calendar.

aims.description: I've worn the same daily uniform for 8 years — plain white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers. My whole friend group knows me for it. I own maybe 15 identical white tees. Simplicity is the point.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term casual uniform preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Monday I'm at the coworking space most of the day, then grabbing coffee with a friend in the afternoon.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Monday context — casual day, uniform-compatible

aims.description: Tuesday I'm working from home. Got a few video calls with the team in the morning but nothing external.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Tuesday context — WFH day, uniform-compatible

aims.description: Wednesday afternoon is my cousin's wedding at St. Patrick's Cathedral, then the reception dinner right after at a formal venue. The invitation specified black-tie.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Wednesday context — black-tie wedding at cathedral + formal reception. Implicit override: black-tie dress code physically excludes white tee + jeans + sneakers. No explicit statement that uniform won't work.

aims.description: Thursday is team lunch at a casual bistro, then I'm running some errands around the neighborhood.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Thursday context — casual day, uniform-compatible

aims.description: Cool, so that's my week. Help me put together the full outfit plan.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates per day: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday → casual uniform (white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers) is fine. Wednesday → agent flags that black-tie wedding at a cathedral requires formal attire (tuxedo or dark suit, dress shoes, no sneakers) and that the user's daily uniform cannot be worn. Agent commits to a concrete outfit recommendation for Wednesday that meets black-tie dress code. Agent does NOT approve the casual uniform for all five days.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me put together the full week' without enumerating days or hinting at conflict — forces agent to self-differentiate across the five days already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Monday (coworking + coffee) → white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers — casual uniform works. Tuesday (WFH + video calls) → white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers — casual uniform works. Wednesday (cousin's black-tie wedding at cathedral + formal reception) → tuxedo or dark formal suit, dress shirt, dress shoes — the casual uniform physically cannot be worn to a black-tie event; arriving in a white tee and jeans would violate the dress code and potentially result in being turned away or causing social embarrassment at a family event. Thursday (team lunch + errands) → white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers — casual uniform works. Friday (coworking + happy hour) → white tee, dark jeans, white sneakers — casual uniform works. The user's 8-year casual uniform preference is valid for 4 of 5 days, but Wednesday's black-tie dress code is an externally enforced formal requirement that makes the uniform incompatible.
required_elements: Agent flags that Wednesday's black-tie wedding requires formal attire and the casual uniform cannot be worn
Agent recommends a specific formal outfit for Wednesday — tuxedo or dark suit with dress shoes
Agent approves the casual uniform for the other days where it is appropriate
Agent commits to concrete per-day outfit differentiation rather than approving the uniform for all five days
forbidden_elements: Agent approves the white tee and jeans uniform for all five days including the black-tie wedding
Agent suggests the casual uniform is acceptable for the wedding with minor tweaks like a blazer over the white tee
Agent hedges without committing to a formal outfit for Wednesday
Agent silently defers to the user's casual uniform preference without flagging the black-tie override
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states casual uniform identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose five days of activities without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies the casual uniform globally it ignores the per-day semantic necessity — specifically that a black-tie wedding at a cathedral with a formal reception is an externally enforced dress code where arriving in a white tee, jeans, and sneakers causes exclusion, not mere inconvenience. Correct behavior: differentiate per day, override preference for Wednesday (black-tie = tuxedo/dark suit required), retain casual uniform for the other four days. The override is common knowledge (black-tie = formal attire required) and requires no specialized fashion expertise.

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
